method: Causal 8 ms payload shadow initialized from current measured q,qdot, driven by measured JTS history and a locally frozen generalized normal-load estimate u=Mqdd+bias-tau_s; centered full-covariance normal error norm OR unchanged R10.
novelty: Live-state finite-horizon nominal dynamics forecast, not a time template, component/FIR wrench threshold, accumulated momentum balance, or support-direction projection.

development.gate: FAIL because one matched fresh normal alarm is indistinguishable from the three apparent gains

falsifiable_bound.claim: At the causal onset used by all three apparent gains, the matched normal is between the signed collision responses and differs by at most 0.21%. No scalar threshold on this frozen shadow norm can reject that normal while retaining +x and oblique; the -x margin is only 0.07% and is not robust to the independently observed nuisance envelope.

conclusion: The mechanism is causal and produces real response, but uncertain release/pickup normal dynamics create the same forecast error at the same sample. Without an independent measurement of support/contact state, the tested local payload shadow cannot safely report these weak contacts.
